facts.raw_span: A 31-year-old woman
presents with a 4-year history of recurrent painful ulcerations on both legs and feet
no personal or family history of vascular or autoimmune disease
denies arthralgia or other dermatologic symptoms
takes no medications
denies tobacco or illicit drug use
a reticular purplish livedo pattern is noted over both lower limbs
Multiple chronic, nonhealing ulcers are present over the lateral malleolus and the dorsum of the left foot
white atrophic scars on the lower legs and ankles
thrombophilia, hematologic malignancies, immune-mediated vasculitis, connective tissue diseases, arterial disease, vascular proliferations, diabetes, and medication-induced ulcers
A lesional skin biopsy was performed

The patient's chronic, nonhealing ulcers and white atrophic scars are consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum, which is a dermatologic condition that can cause skin ulcers and scarring.
The patient's recurrent painful ulcerations and livedo pattern are consistent with thrombophilia, which is a hematologic disorder that can cause blood clots and skin lesions.

The patient's recurrent painful ulcerations and livedo pattern are consistent with immune-mediated vasculitis, which is an immune-mediated disorder that can cause blood vessel inflammation and skin lesions.
The patient's chronic, nonhealing ulcers are consistent with diabetes mellitus, which is a metabolic disorder that can cause skin ulcers and other complications.
The patient's livedo pattern is consistent with livedoid vasculopathy, which is a vascular disorder that can cause skin lesions and ulcers.

The patient's recurrent painful ulcerations and livedo pattern are consistent with Wegener's granulomatosis, which is an immune-mediated disorder that can cause blood vessel inflammation and skin lesions.
The patient's recurrent painful ulcerations and livedo pattern are consistent with polyarteritis nodosa, which is a vascular disorder that can cause blood vessel inflammation and skin lesions.
